subject: HelioHealth SLO discovery — context ceilings, streaming and next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: HelioHealth SLO discovery — context ceilings, streaming and next steps

Hi Emma — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment.

Summary of asks (from call):
- Desired latency: p95 <= 250ms for single-turn generation in product UI (interactive assistant).
- Typical concurrency target: 600 concurrent active users (peaks to ~1,200/session-backed requests).
- Streaming: yes — partial token streaming for improved perceived latency is required.
- Context window: inbound customer data up to ~12k tokens (mix of short & one long document), expected generation output up to ~3k tokens in worst-case summaries.
- Cost sensitivity: product team wants to understand Dedicated vs Hosted unit economics for sustained traffic.

Ask from us: please send a representative token distribution/sequence-length CSV and any latency target slack (e.g., acceptable p95 or p99) so we can size the perf POC.

I attached a simple template (helio_token_profile.xlsx) you can drop data into. Proposed immediate next steps:
1) You paste the token distribution into our template (we can also map if you send a sample payload).
2) We run a 10–14 day perf POC (hosted or dedicated) exercising streaming and 12k context read paths.
3) Deliverables: p50/p95/p99 latency curves by sequence length, concurrency runbook, and cost estimate for steady-state vs burst.

Proposed meeting: Tue 2027-04-26 11:00 PT for kickoff / technical scoping. Does that work?

Thanks —
Markus

Date: 2027-04-22T17:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HelioHealth SLO discovery — context ceilings, streaming and next steps

Markus — thanks for the recap and the template. Quick clarifications from product and infra:

1) Latency tolerance: product team wants p95 <= 200–300ms on typical queries (short prompts). For long-context summarization (12k in, ~3k out) they can accept p95 up to 1.2s but prefer <800ms if possible.
2) Concurrency: baseline is 600 concurrent UI sessions but the team expects spikes to 1.1k for marketing-driven events. They want graceful degradation rather than hard failures.
3) Streaming: absolutely required for the UI UX. Partial token streaming must start within ~120–200ms of request acceptance for short prompts.
4) Data residency: US only for this PoC.

I've attached a sample export from our staging service with token frequency histograms and a short sample payload (we redacted PII). Please confirm if you need us to provide raw payloads or an anonymized sampling will do.

Procurement is CC'd — they want a high-level cost ballpark before committing to a dedicated trial.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Li
Senior PM, HelioHealth
emma@heliohealth.com
Attachment: helio_sample_token_export.csv
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-23T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: HelioHealth SLO discovery — internal next steps and POC plan

Team — internal plan based on Emma's reply (copied below for context). Key points and asks:

- Requirements summary: p95 short prompts target 200–300ms, long summaries up to 1.2s acceptable, streaming required (start <200ms). Concurrency 600 steady / 1100 spikes. Context read path frequently hits ~12k tokens.

- Proposed Redwood POC scope:
  * Mode: Hosted perf qualification initially (to prove feasibility quickly) with optional Dedicated sizing after results.
  * Test matrix: sequence lengths [256, 1024, 4096, 8192, 12288], outputs [128, 512, 2048, 3072], concurrency sweep [50, 200, 600, 1,200].
  * Streaming validation: measure time-to-first-byte and token-rate under the same sweep.
  * SLO checks: p50/p95/p99 per-candidate config and fallback policy defined (e.g., shorter context variant, cache prefixes).
  * Fallback behavior: automatic model-variant fallback to lower-context (8k) with best-effort summary concatenation for degraded conditions.

- Immediate asks: Connor — can you draft the perf POC job spec (tools, runbook, cost/rate limits) and estimate the run hours / GPU-hours for hosted sims?
- Monica — can you prepare a short cost comparator (hosted vs dedicated) that factors in sustained 600 concurrent and a reserved-of-peak scenario (committed 800 concurrency) for 6 months?

I will assemble the POC doc and send a consolidated PDF + cost ballpark to Emma/Procurement by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Emma — quick update and proposed kickoff plan.

1) Attached: Redwood perf POC plan (redwood_perf_poc_plan.pdf) and an initial cost estimate (cost_estimate_draft.xlsx). These include the test matrix Aisha outlined and a preliminary GPU-hour estimate for hosted runs.

2) Scope: 10 business days of active runs + 2 days for analysis and delivery. We will run the full sequence-length sweep and streaming validation at target concurrencies (50 / 200 / 600 / 1,200). For the streaming SLA we will measure time-to-first-byte and sustained token throughput to ensure perceived latency <200ms for short prompts.

3) Fallbacks & throttling: plan includes automatic prefix/cache and model-variant fallback to keep service responsive during spikes. We'll validate graceful degradation rather than hard 429s.

4) Next steps for you: please confirm (A) which deployment you'd prefer for the POC (Hosted quick-qual vs Dedicated trial), and (B) provide the token-distribution CSV or allow us to sample from staging. Procurement — if you want a short statement of work (SOW) / MOP to review before kickoff, we can draft one pending a high-level cost agreement.

Proposed kickoff: Tue 2027-04-26 11:00 PT — confirm and we'll send calendar invite + preread.
